claims.claim: The game cannot adjust its window size, requiring resolution adjustments in Windows settings to make the window easier to see.

citations.review_text:
Really enjoying this game! Lots of 4th wall breaking elements. My only suggestion would be to possibly add a way to make the window larger. 

EDIT: OK, just finished the game. Absolutely incredible love letter to The Little Prince! I regret sleeping on it for so long but I'm glad I finally picked it up. Do yourself a favor and don't pass on this little gem!!

I kept hearing about how great this game was and all that, so I decided to buy it while it was on sale. After playing through, I can say without a doubt: This game is amazing. The music, pixel art, story, characters, everything is done so awesomely. The narrative is superrrr compelling and the characters actually mean something to the player. I think this is a game that wayyyy more people should play and I enjoyed the unique puzzle solving present in this game. Before playing though, make sure you quit out of anything like wallpaper engine ;D. I also needed to adjust the resolution of my monitor in my Windows settings in order to make the game window easier to see, as you can't adjust the window size itself (which actually works in favor of this game's aforementioned unique puzzle solving). All in all, a great game!! I love Niko!!!!!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that exploring the large map involves considerable wandering and going back and forth, which can lead to getting lost.

citations.review_text:
Oneshot is a top-down adventure made with the RPGMaker engine although it doesn't look like a RPGMaker game because it uses mostly custom original assets. So not graphically impressive but interesting art design with some nifty special effects (such as fireflies in the Barrens). The gameplay is mostly exploring, talking and solving puzzles; there is no combat. The game was intriguing overall and sometimes challenging. Heck, I was stuck in the first room.  I was also stuck because I had a program automatically changing wallpapers on my computer. So keep that in mind and that a few puzzles require thinking "outside the box". I applaud their originality. There was also a very cool surprise reveal when you encountered your first talking person that made the proceedings way more personal.

The writing was good, but item descriptions were too brief, and I wish I could have become more emotionally invested. It was easy to get get lost while exploring, but there was that Travel button to important places you had been which I appreciated. At the end, I found Oneshot good, even very good, and I give it points for originality and storytelling, but I was also a bit disappointed, as if something was missing. However, something I discovered later on elevated the game to remarkable and memorable status. I'll mention that spoiler in the comment box below with spoiler tags but only check it out after you've finished the game.

P.S. Another newer version of this game exists called "World Machine" edition, but I suggest playing this version here if you're on PC.

I didn't know a thing about OneShot in the least when I booted it up last night. All I knew was that this game was rated overwhelmingly positive on steam, and from what little information I could glean from the steam description.

This game is overwhelmingly phenomenal, and completely deserving of all the high praise it's received.

I wound up blasting through the entire thing in one sitting, no breaks, and no google searches in about five and a half hours, and I loved every bit of it.

The puzzles are well thought out, if a little time-consuming (having to go back and forth and back and forth over and over again is a pain, even if you can fast travel, along with the fact that you might have just missed the one particular thing you need to finish the puzzle along the way, especially on some of the bigger maps). Nothing is wasted, and everything is given it's moment to shine. Puzzles have always been very hit-or-miss for me, but these were a major hit. (with a couple notable exceptions)

The game doesn't treat the player as a nonexistent observer. The player, as well as your computer itself, is integrated into the game as their own character and setting, which only served to further my immersion into the game's story. Chances are, if you've played or are looking at this game, you've played other titles like Doki Doki Literature Club, which also messes with your PC files and breaks the fourth wall. This game not only did that earlier, but did it better.

Out of every game I've played that breaks the fourth wall, OneShot is by far the best. They seamlessly weave each break into the story and narrative without feeling jarring or breaking pace or immersion, and it really does keep you on your toes. (P.S. if you have Wallpaper Engine running, turn it off while you're playing this game, trust me.)

The writing is fantastic. Every character is likeable while also being unique in their own different ways, Niko, our protagonist, is a phenomenal main character and absolutely p…

To be honest, I’m not capable of writing a polished, stellar review, so I’ll just ramble casually, haha.
 
For me, this is an outstanding game. It made me realise I am not merely an observer, but an active participant in the story. Through the screen, I guided Niko along their journey, spoke with them in dreams, and slowly came to understand Niko’s longing for home and for their mother. Atop the tower, Niko placed their own fate into my hands.
 
On one side lies light for an entire world; on the other, a child’s wish to return home. There is no standard answer, no absolutely correct choice. The decision I make cannot be undone — I only get one chance.
 
Let’s talk about the puzzles: The riddles in OneShot rely heavily on various clues presented within the game itself.
 
As for the narrative, as I mentioned above, the writing is phenomenal. In my opinion, it stands shoulder-to-shoulder with Undertale. The creative meta elements, the unique bond you share with Niko, well-developed NPCs, and those mysterious interactions that extend beyond the game window onto your desktop create an incredibly distinctive experience.
 
Here are some random afterthoughts:
The game’s map is enormous. When I first started playing, I did not even know fast travel existed; I must have missed that hint in the story. Solving puzzles often sends Niko trekking back and forth across long stretches. Without walkthroughs, many sections would be extremely tough to get through. Carefully reading all in-game text is absolutely vital.
 
Truth be told, I hesitated for nearly fifteen minutes on the choice screen at the lighthouse. If I hadn’t watched videos beforehand and learned multiple endings exist, I would have likely lingered on that screen indefinitely, unable to make up my mind.
 
One small tip: If you plan to buy and play it, follow the game’s suggestion and avoid fullscreen mode. You’ll understand why once you experience it for yoursel

NO SPOILERS

Excellent story i love it. Played it after seeing Indie Cross (Youtube series). Did not disappoint lots of wandering if that's not your thing. One of those games where it is NOT the same watching it then playing it. (i think half the fandom is Undertale/Deltarune fans including me)

NOT RECOMMENDED IF YOU ARE PARANOID

If you are thinking about getting this game DO IT (best played spoiler free)

For the whole game experience i recommend playing the game (since there are a lot of 4th wall breaks).

Like most of the Indie games, the OST is PHENOMENAL. There's no need explaining it. It just fits the game perfectly.

I wasn't really feeling it even after finishing it....But then Solstice happened and yeah I'd firmly say it's a solid indie game.
It has absorbing atmosphere , the story  is tied to being really 4th wall breaking and it has some cool actual PC gimmicks you have to follow to continue with the game. Vibe was also really nice with soundtrack that complimented the  whole world the entire time.
That being said perhaps I've seen and read enough but I did not feel the emotional scenes all that much. 
Regardless of me not feeling the emotional scenes all that much , the ending of Solstice was pretty  good. I liked it. 
7/10

"You only get OneShot."
OneShot isn't just an RPG Maker game—it's an experience that breaks the boundary between you and your monitor. Instead of playing as Niko, you are acting as Niko's guide, helping a lost child navigate a dying world with a lightbulb in hand.
What sets this game apart is its incredible meta-gameplay. Puzzles leak out of the game window and onto your actual desktop in ways that are genuinely mind-blowing and clever. Coupled with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack, a melancholic atmosphere, and an unforgettable protagonist, it creates an emotional bond few games ever manage to achieve. And there's a reason why it's called OneShot.
If you love games like Undertale, OFF, or OMORI, do not skip this. Go in completely blind.
10/10 — Protect Niko at all costs.

One of the rare few games that could reasonably be considered masterpieces. The use of meta elements is brilliant, the character designs are well-made, the story and its twists are foreshadowed well without feeling obvious, and it's all-around just excellent.

One of the best games I've ever played <3
Incredible story, the meta aspect of the game and features are something you don't find often in other games, the game's awesome.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking replay value because the story does not have the same impact a second time.

citations.review_text:
For a game that's 10 years old by now, I feel like the story holds up better than even newer games. It is not a game for everyone, especially if you're not into this kind of indie genre, but personally I loved the whole world design, as well as the story. Would I replay this game? Unfortunately no. The story doesn't hit the same as it does the first time, and the game's name is pretty tight in the meaning. One Shot at saving the world and experiencing it's story. Even if there's a feature to replay the game, replaying it doesn't change much unless you have other things to discover. There's also The World Machine Edition which offers you more content than the original remake, but modding that version is a bit more difficult than it is to mod the remake. Anyway, I'd say if you never experienced this game nor have you ever knew anything about it, the story might change you a little and it's worth the money even at full price.

(P.S. I usually don't cry at games but this game really made me cry at the very end. Pick putting the sun back, you'll see why.)
I loved every bit of it, the story, the cuteness all of it, would play again just for funnsies ^^
